reflections.summary: The loss stemmed from a flawed team-preview choice: bringing a Sun-dependent core (Torkoal/Metagross) against a dedicated Rain lead (Politoed/Archaludon) allowed a rain-boosted Electro Shot to instantly remove Metagross, while predictable double Protects stalled Torkoal’s Eruption and Politoed’s Ice Beam chipped it down to a Final Gambit KO.
reflections.adjustment: Swap Metagross for a faster Electric-immune or Water-resistant pivot (or a non-Sun Mega) to neutralize the Drizzle lead; when double Protect is anticipated, pivot to switching or status instead of committing to blocked attacks, and preserve Torkoal’s HP above the Final Gambit threshold.
reflections.notebook: Sun vs rain war is series-defining: Torkoal Drought must overcome Politoed Drizzle. Opponent aggressively leads Politoed + Archaludon to exploit rain-boosted Electro Shot; Metagross is highly vulnerable to this core. Opponent uses double Protect to stall Eruption/Fake Out; pivot to switching or status when anticipated. Staraptor's Final Gambit targets low-HP Torkoal; maintain HP threshold or bring faster revenge killer. Politoed Sitrus triggers at 50%. Future plan: Bring dedicated rain counter (Electric immunity/faster weather setter) and avoid Sun-reliant leads against Drizzle cores.

reflections.summary: Won despite losing Archaludon to a critical-hit Earth Power on turn 4. Staraptor's Intimidate, Close Combat KO on Incineroar, and Final Gambit KO on Torkoal closed the game. Scizor-Mega was effectively dead weight — 4x Fire-weak under Drought and never fielded — so the win was carried entirely by Staraptor + Politoed.
reflections.adjustment: Re-evaluate bringing Scizor-Mega against any team with Torkoal sun; it cannot safely switch in and contributed nothing. Consider a Mega that isn't Fire-weak or a fourth slot that actively pressures sun cores.
